query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Addition of rare earth elements to single-phase fcc FeCoNi will increase the coercive field by enhancing magnetic anisotropy.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its high-entropy alloy derivatives
generation.intervention: Addition of rare earth elements (e.g., Nd, Dy, or Pr) to the alloy composition
generation.structural_mediator: Magnetic anisotropy induced by rare earth elements
generation.mechanism: Enhanced magnetic anisotropy leading to increased coercive field
generation.predicted_outcome: Increase in coercive field by a factor of 2-5 relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its matched derivatives
generation.baseline: Coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its matched derivatives (<= 100 Oe)
generation.boundary: Composition: 1-5 at.% rare earth elements; Structure: single-phase fcc; Measurement: magnetic hysteresis loop at room temperature
generation.uncertainty: Actual increase in coercive field may vary depending on specific rare earth element and concentration

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloys with and without rare earth element additions (e.g., 2 at.% Nd). Measure magnetic hysteresis loops at room temperature.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the alloy with rare earth element addition is not significantly higher (by a factor of 2-5) than that of the alloy without rare earth element addition, the hypothesis is falsified.
